quickSummary: Ionization Enthalpy (Δ_i H) increases across a period and decreases down a group, but displays sharp subshell anomalies in Period 2 (Be > B, N > O), Group 13 (B > Tl > Ga > Al > In), and Group 14 (Pb > Sn).
summary: Master Ionization Enthalpy trends, governing quantum factors, subshell exchange stability anomalies, and group contraction impacts.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Ionization Enthalpy Definition & Factors
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Ionization Enthalpy Definition & Factors

summaryBox.title: Ionization Enthalpy
summaryBox.takeaway: Minimum energy to remove most loosely bound electron from isolated neutral gaseous atom. Δ_i H₁ < Δ_i H₂ < Δ_i H₃ < ... < Δ_i H_n.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Ionization enthalpy is endothermic ($\Delta_i H > 0$):

$$\text{X}(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta_i H_1} \text{X}^+(g) + e^- \quad (\Delta_i H_1 > 0)$$
$$\mathbf{\Delta_i H_1 < \Delta_i H_2 < \Delta_i H_3 < \dots < \Delta_i H_n}$$

• **Governing Factors**:
1. **Atomic Size**: $\Delta_i H \propto \frac{1}{r}$.
2. **Effective Nuclear Charge**: $\Delta_i H \propto Z_{\text{eff}}$.
3. **Electronic Configuration Stability**: Extra stability of fully-filled ($s^2, p^6, d^{10}$) and half-filled ($p^3, d^5$) subshells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Subshell Anomalies in Periods & Groups
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Subshell Anomalies in Periods & Groups
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PERIOD 2 IONIZATION ENTHALPY ANOMALIES
                       
   IE₁(Be) > IE₁(B):  Be (1s² 2s²) has fully-filled s-subshell & 2s penetration vs B (2p¹).
   IE₁(N) > IE₁(O):   N (2p³) possesses stable half-filled 2p³ subshell vs O (2p⁴).

   Period 2 Order: Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne
   Period 3 Order: Na < Al < Mg < Si < S < P < Cl < Ar
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Period 2 Trend**: $\mathbf{\text{Li} < \text{B} < \text{Be} < \text{C} < \text{O} < \text{N} < \text{F} < \text{Ne}}$
- $\text{Be} > \text{B}$: $\text{Be } (2s^2)$ has higher $2s$ penetration and fully-filled stability vs $\text{B } (2p^1)$.
- $\text{N} > \text{O}$: $\text{N } (2p^3)$ has stable half-filled subshell with high exchange energy vs $\text{O } (2p^4)$.

• **Group 13 Trend**: Irregular due to $3d^{10}$ Scandide and $4f^{14}$ Lanthanide contractions:
$$\mathbf{\text{B } (801) > \text{Tl } (589) > \text{Ga } (579) > \text{Al } (577) > \text{In } (558\text{ kJ/mol})}$$

• **Group 14 Trend**: Lead ($\text{Pb}$) has higher $\Delta_i H_1$ than Tin ($\text{Sn}$) due to $4f^{14}$ Lanthanide contraction:
$$\mathbf{\text{C} > \text{Si} > \text{Ge} > \text{Pb } (715\text{ kJ/mol}) > \text{Sn } (708\text{ kJ/mol})}$$

quickRevision: Successive IEs always increase: Δ_i H₁ < Δ_i H₂ < Δ_i H₃.
Period 2 IE: Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne.
Period 3 IE: Na < Al < Mg < Si < S < P < Cl < Ar.
Group 13 IE: B > Tl > Ga > Al > In (Ga > Al and Tl > In due to contractions).
Group 14 IE: C > Si > Ge > Pb > Sn (Pb > Sn due to Lanthanide contraction).
